name: pwm_fpga_demo
description: Single-clock FPGA-friendly PWM LED demo for board prototyping. The design generates a visible breathing/fading pattern on one LED by combining a slow rate divider/counter, an 8-bit PWM counter, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a direction bit. The implementation is intended to be synthesizable in open-source Lattice FPGA flows such as Yosys and nextpnr, with no ASIC-only or testbench-only constructs.

fixed_assumptions: No explicit reset input is required; internal registers initialize to known values only if supported by the target synthesis flow, otherwise the design must be allowed to power up in a safe, non-deterministic but synthesizable state and self-stabilize by counting.
The PWM pattern shall be visibly slow on a typical 50 MHz board clock by using a slow counter-derived update event.
Board-specific starter pin constraints are intentionally not embedded in RTL and must be created after the target board is selected, using PCF for iCE40 and LPF for ECP5.

functionality: Generate a continuously repeating breathing LED effect. On each system clock, an 8-bit PWM counter increments free-running and is compared against an 8-bit duty-cycle register to produce the LED output. A slow counter creates a periodic update event that advances the duty cycle by one step at a much lower rate. A direction bit controls whether the duty cycle ramps upward or downward between 0x00 and 0xFF, causing the LED brightness to fade in and out smoothly and visibly. The top module must remain a compact, fully synthesizable RTL description suitable for linting, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, timing analysis, and bitstream handoff.
responsibilities: Accept the board clock on clk.
Generate an 8-bit PWM carrier counter internally.
Generate a slow timing event from an internal divider/counter.
Maintain an 8-bit duty-cycle register that ramps up and down.
Maintain a direction bit indicating increment versus decrement.
Drive led with the PWM comparison result.
Avoid any non-synthesizable constructs, vendor primitives, memories, delays, or real-number operations.
must_not_drive: Any reset input, because none is defined.
Any vendor-specific pin or primitive instance.
reset_behavior: No explicit reset port is defined. The RTL should be written so that, in the absence of reset, the design still synthesizes cleanly and the breathing pattern self-runs from its initial or power-up state. Internal counters, duty-cycle register, and direction bit should be arranged to avoid unsafe LED behavior and to converge into a valid triangular brightness sweep.
behavior_rules: Use exactly one input clock named clk.
Use exactly one LED output named led.
Implement a free-running 8-bit PWM counter that increments every clock cycle.
Implement a slow counter or divider to generate a visible update tick for the duty-cycle ramp.
Implement an 8-bit duty-cycle register that increments or decrements by one at each slow update tick.
Implement a direction bit that flips when the duty-cycle register reaches either full-low or full-high limit.
Clamp or reflect the duty cycle at the boundaries 8'h00 and 8'hFF so the breathing effect repeats endlessly.
Drive led high when the PWM counter is below the duty-cycle register and low otherwise.
Ensure all logic is synchronous and synthesizable for open-source Lattice FPGA flows.
Keep the top module self-contained with no internal hierarchy required.
